newsitem.title: CHINA: China's non-state sector booming - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China's non-state sector booming - newspaper.

text.p: China's non-state sector is growing far faster than official figures show, despite inadequate legal protection and uneven development, the China Economic Times said.

The registered funds of non-state enterprise, which include, private, foreign-invested and individual firms, accounted for 38.4 percent of the total registered funds for enterprises in China at the end of 1995, the newspaper said in an edition available in Beijing on Wednesday.
The non-state sector accounted for 11.6 percent of employment, it said but gave no more details.
"Growth in the private economy is particularly fierce," the newspaper quoted official analysts as saying.
By the end of 1995, China had 46,270 private enterprises each with registered funds of more than 1.0 million yuan ($120,000), soaring 136.8 percent compared with the year before, it said.
Among the main problems facing the non-state sector was the fact that many firms were not included in macro-economic planning, it said.

Legal protection and guidance for the non-state sector was inadequate and development was uneven both in terms of geographic distribution and industry, with eastern areas over-represented and primary industry neglected.
Official statistics failed to fully reflect the growth of the non-state sector, it said.
A 1994 official investigation found that the number of private enterprises masquerading as collective firms was triple the registered number of private firms.
